# Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection (2024-11-26)

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NetBIOS name; AD domain `NEMOTODES` / DNS suffix `nemotoads.health`, DC = 10.11.26.3 / NEMOTODES-DC) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (observed as Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between the host and the domain controller 10.11.26.3) |

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client abused as a commodity RAT).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, on two independent bases:
- Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Independently verified in raw packet payloads pulled from the pcap: the HTTP POST bodies to the C2 use NetSupport's known plaintext client protocol, e.g. `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encoded blob>`, sent to `/fakeurl.htm` — a well-known NetSupport RAT URI artifact.

## 3. Timeline / Infection Vector (as observed in traffic)

- 04:50:11–04:50:40 UTC: 10.11.26.183 resolves and makes TLS connections (SNI) to two lure domains associated with fake/cracked-software download pages: **classicgrand.com** (213.246.109.5:443) and **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139:443, flagged by ET as a "ZPHP Domain" in both DNS and TLS SNI).
- 04:50:45 UTC, seconds after the last lure-domain connection: NetSupport RAT check-in traffic begins to 194.180.191.64:443, and continues as regular ~60-second beacons for the remainder of the capture (04:50 through at least 09:43 local/+0400, i.e. ~05:43 UTC).
- No dropper executable, installer, or archive was captured being downloaded in this pcap (only C2 protocol data, a GeoIP lookup, and routine cert-revocation/OCSP fetches were transferred) — the capture starts at/after initial compromise, so the delivery binary itself is not directly recoverable from this evidence. The lure-domain-then-immediate-RAT-checkin sequence is the strongest evidence of vector in this capture.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2, HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, ~60s beacon interval, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` protocol
- `104.26.1.231:80` — `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, GET `/location/loca.asp` (NetSupport's own geolocation service, queried by the implant; response body: `33.7488,-84.3877`)

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` (resolves to 193.42.38.139) — cracked-software lure domain, flagged ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP
- `classicgrand.com` (resolves to 213.246.109.5) — same lure-domain cluster
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — legitimate NetSupport infrastructure, abused by the RAT client

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 beacon/check-in endpoint)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp`

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. No executable, script, or archive payload was transferred over any protocol in this capture; all attacker-side traffic present is C2 beacon/check-in data (plaintext `CMD=POLL` / encoded `CMD=ENCD` blobs), not file transfer, so no SHA256 can be produced from this evidence.

## 5. Secondary Observations (not attributed to the RAT)

Several SMB/NTLM alerts (`ET INFO Potentially unsafe SMBv1 protocol in use`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt`, `[MS-EFSR] EfsRpcOpenFileRaw`) were logged between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller 10.11.26.3 shortly before the RAT beaconing started. These involve SMBv1/NTLMSSP/EFSRPC activity worth flagging for follow-up (EfsRpcOpenFileRaw calls are notable in relayed-authentication attack chains), but nothing in the captured payloads ties them to the NetSupport RAT itself — recommend separate investigation.

## 6. Recommended Actions

- Isolate DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183) from the network immediately.
- Reset credentials for user `oboomwald` and review the account for AD abuse.
- Block C2 indicator 194.180.191.64 and lure domains modandcrackedapk.com / classicgrand.com at the perimeter.
- Acquire a disk/memory image of the host — this pcap alone cannot recover the dropper binary or a file hash; endpoint forensics are needed to identify patient-zero delivery mechanism and any additional payloads.
